decisions.reason: Although polymer concrete extends beyond the firm's traditional metal base, the product is still close to its drainage know-how and its own web page in both 2018 and 2019 suggests sufficient early traction to keep learning and improving it.

A floor-level shower drainage system fits very closely with the firm's existing drainage knowledge, and its move from a mention in 2018 to its own page in 2019 indicates strengthening market acceptance.

This designer shower drainage product is technologically close to the firm's core capabilities, but its reduced prominence in 2019 points to more uncertain demand and therefore a moderate but not decisive drop risk.

The shower element with integrated slope complements the firm's drainage business and can benefit from existing customer and installer knowledge, yet its limited visibility suggests a weaker standalone case than the main drainage lines.

The backflow-protected basement floor drain is a strongly core drainage product and its explicit development emphasis plus home-page visibility in 2019 imply that the firm sees clear value and has strong capability to exploit it further.

An air-admittance valve is related to sanitary systems but is less central to the firm's strongest drainage-specific knowledge base, and its low web prominence gives management weaker evidence that further internal learning will pay off.
